newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle seen steady to off, feeders mixed.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle seen steady to off, feeders mixed.

text.p: CME live cattle futures were expected to open steady to 0.150 cent per lb higher while calls on feeder cattle futures ranged mixed, from 0.200 cent higher to 0.200 lower, livestock analysts said.

Although expectations abound that cash beef prices are close to bottoming, lower boxed beef values again late Friday were viewed as a selling factor. Carryover of part of the showlist was also considered a selling factor, analysts said.
Bulls have been looking for beef prices to rebound as the grilling season gets under way, but weather conditions were not that favorable over the past weekend, they said.

Feeder cattle futures calls ranged mixed with some analysts looking for carryover strength linked to another gain in the latest CME feeder cattle index. Poor calving weather should also be supportive to deferred contracts.
But others cited expected weakness in live cattle futures and calls for higher corn futures which may pressure the market, analysts said.
The latest CME feeder cattle index was quoted up $0.30 at $70.81 per cwt, the highest level in over two years, since March 1, 1995.
